result:
No — don't cut production over this week. Marketing claims ("99.9% accuracy," "SOC2 compliant," case studies) aren't evidence of how the API performs on *your* content and edge cases, and moderation failures have real safety/trust/legal blast radius if you're wrong.

Before switching, I'd want:
- **Verify SOC2, don't take it on faith** — ask for the actual SOC2 Type II report (Type I just means controls exist, not that they were tested over time), and check it covers the moderation service itself, not just their infra.
- **Test against your own labeled data** — "99.9% accuracy" is meaningless without knowing their test set, class balance, and what counts as a "miss." Run it against a sample of your real traffic (including your known hard cases/adversarial content) and compare precision/recall to your current provider.
- **Check the case studies critically** — do those customers have similar content types/volume to you, and are the results third-party verified or vendor-written?
- **Shadow it first** — run the new API in parallel (log-only, not decisioning) against live traffic for a week or two before it touches production, so you catch failure modes before users do.

Given the pricing is attractive, this is worth pursuing — just not as a same-week production cutover. Want help drafting a shadow-mode test harness or an eval script to compare the two providers on a sample of your data?
